svg.title: Create the private practice network — instructional mockup
svg.desc: Step-specific guided recreation. Not a genuine screenshot or live result.
svg.text: INSTRUCTIONAL MOCKUP — NOT A LIVE CAPTURE OR RESULT
Create the private practice network
Your Windows 10 host · VMware Workstation Pro 17
RHEL 9 — learner@tls-app01
COMMAND / FILE CONTENT TO ENTER — PRESERVE CASE
sudo shutdown -h now
EXPECTED RESULT / SIMULATED CLUE — CHECK YOUR OWN MACHINE
Both powered-off VMs use only VMnet6; Windows has a VMnet6 address of 10.90.0.254.
FOLLOW THE NUMBERED INSTRUCTIONS IN THE LESSON
1. At each Linux console, run the shutdown command below. Wait until both VMs show Powered off.
2. In VMware, choose Edit, then Virtual Network Editor. Click Change Settings and accept the Windows
administrator prompt.
3. Click Add Network, choose VMnet6 if unused, then OK. Select Host-only, set Subnet IP to 10.90.0.0 and
Subnet mask to 255.255.255.0.
4. Enable Connect a host virtual adapter to this network. Clear Use local DHCP service to distribute IP
addresses to VMs. Click Apply, then OK.
5. For each VM, open Edit virtual machine settings, select Network Adapter, choose Custom: VMnet6, and
save. Each VM must have exactly one adapter; no NAT or Bridged adapter remains.
6. On Windows, press Win+R, type ncpa.cpl and press Enter. Right-click VMware Network Adapter VMnet6,
choose Properties, select Internet Protocol Version 4, and click Properties. Set address 10.90.0.254,
mask 255.255.255.0, and leave gateway and DNS blank. Do not edit your physical Wi-Fi or Ethernet
adapter.
No real private key, real certificate result, production access or DoD endorsement is shown.
